evidence.quote: The byway begins at Calico Rock and proceeds along Highways 5 and 14 and Forest Service Road 110 to Blanchard Springs Caverns.

evidence.claim: ARDOT identifies it as a Forest Service Scenic Byway and highlights white oak-hickory forests, early spring dogwoods and redbuds, and fall color.
evidence.quote: The Sylamore Scenic Byway is a Forest Service Scenic Byway located in the southeast corner of the Ozark National Forest.

evidence.claim: ARDOT identifies it as a Forest Service Scenic Byway and highlights white oak-hickory forests, early spring dogwoods and redbuds, and fall color.
evidence.quote: The white oak-hickory forests provide an early spring view of dogwoods and redbuds and majestic fall color.

evidence.claim: The route received its National Forest Scenic Byway designation in 1989.
evidence.quote: The Sylamore Scenic Byway was designated as a National Forest Scenic Byway on February 8, 1989.

evidence.claim: Its cave destination had opened to the public in 1973 after ten years of work on the Dripstone Trail.
evidence.quote: The caverns were opened to the public in 1973 after 10 years of development on the Dripstone Trail.

evidence.claim: Earlier recreation work remains at nearby Mirror Lake: a Civilian Conservation Corps crew dammed the creek from Blanchard Spring in 1940, and the historic district includes their observation shelter and a CCC-built bridge.
evidence.quote: The lake was created by a crew of the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1940 by damming the creek emanating from Blanchard Spring. The district includes the lake, the dam, and two bridges, one of which was also built by the CCC, and a CCC-built observation shelter nearby.

evidence.claim: Drive south from Calico Rock through Optimus, following the White River toward Allison.
evidence.quote: Allison near the White River. The Sylamore Creek Byway begins an overlap with Highway 5 and Highway 9 northbound, following the White River and passing the Miles Jeffery Barn. It passes through Optimus, an unincorporated community, before terminating at a bridge over the White River.

evidence.claim: There, turn west onto winding Highway 14, then take the forest road to the caverns’ visitor center.
evidence.quote: The Sylamore Scenic Byway begins at the National Forest Service Blanchard Springs Caverns Visitor Center. The Mirror Lake Historic District is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The route runs west along Forest Highway 1110. It turns onto Highway 14, which winds east past an intersection with Highway 87 to Allison near the White River.

evidence.claim: Four main cables carry the Sylamore Creek suspension bridge, supported by steel towers on concrete piers and anchored into concrete abutments.
evidence.quote: It is a wire-cable suspension bridge, with steel towers mounted on concrete piers supporting four main cables that are anchored into concrete abutments.

evidence.claim: Built in 1945, the 202-foot bridge crosses the creek on County Road 283, just west of Highway 9 in Allison.
evidence.quote: It carries County Road 283 across Sylamore Creek, a short way west of Arkansas Highway 9 and north of the Holiday Mountain Resort in Allison.

evidence.claim: Residents knew the place as Half-Mile Cave by the 1930s, before systematic exploration began in the 1950s.
evidence.quote: Residents knew about the cave by the 1930s and called it Half-Mile Cave. Systematic explorations began in the 1950s

evidence.claim: Ten years of development on the Dripstone Trail preceded the public opening in 1973.
evidence.quote: The caverns were opened to the public in 1973 after 10 years of development on the Dripstone Trail.

evidence.claim: The cave formed largely below the water table, producing passages with elliptical cross-sections.
evidence.quote: The cave's formation was largely phreatic in nature (formed below the water table) and passages have elliptical cross-sections typical of these formations.

evidence.claim: Its stream emerges at Blanchard Springs at a constant 58 degrees Fahrenheit, the same temperature as the cave throughout the year.
evidence.quote: The present stream currently rises from the cave at Blanchard Springs itself, at the same temperature as the cave, a constant, year-round 58 °F (14 °C).

evidence.claim: The upper Dripstone route opened first; the Discovery Trail followed in 1977, descending to the lower cave.
evidence.quote: The Dripstone Trail runs through the uppermost level of caverns for about a 0.5 miles (0.80 km) and opened in 1973. The Discovery Trail opened in 1977 and loops through a 1.2 miles (1.9 km) section of the cavern, descending to the lower level of the cave
